overall: Committee impermissibly relied on the Open Meeting Law to keep withholding parts of three 2012–2013 executive session minutes after the purposes were served; collective bargaining redaction upheld, privilege and Purpose 7 claims rejected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee improperly withheld portions of several executive session minutes and documents used at those sessions, including the investigation report.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the Committee can no longer rely on the Open Meeting Law’s Purpose 1 to withhold section of its August 27, 2012, December 18, 2012, and February 5, 2013, executive session minutes that relate to the complaint against the Superintendent.

allegations.summary: Committee withheld a paragraph of December 2012 minutes under Purpose 3 (collective bargaining), saying release would harm future bargaining with a faculty union.
allegations.key_passage: We agree that the publication of that portion of the minutes could have a detrimental effect on the public body’s collective bargaining position in future negotiations with the MFA.

allegations.summary: Committee withheld a sentence about prior grievances under Purpose 3, though the minutes only recorded that a question was asked and the answer was deferred.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee has not adequately justified the need for continued nondisclosure of this sentence.

allegations.summary: Committee redacted paragraphs of minutes citing Purpose 7 and attorney-client privilege; privilege cannot support a Purpose 7 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The protection of the attorney-client privilege is not a valid basis for claiming applicability of executive session Purpose 7.

allegations.summary: Committee asserted attorney-client privilege to withhold portions of minutes; the AG said the OML gives it no authority to decide whether the privilege was properly claimed.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not authorize the Attorney General to determine whether the Committee’s assertion of the attorney-client privilege was justified.

allegations.summary: Committee relied on Public Records Law exemptions to keep redactions; the AG said disputes over those exemptions belong with the Supervisor of Records.
allegations.key_passage: we offer no opinion on whether any exemptions in the Public Records Law may authorize withholding those documents.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
Publicly release the sentence on page 1 of the December 18, 2012 minutes under item “a. Follow up on grievances,” unless the attorney-client privilege or a Public Records Law exemption applies.
Disclose portions of its executive session minutes in accordance with the order.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
